recipes.name: Quick Lobster Bisque
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon seafood seasoning (such as Old Bay®)

steps.text: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Stir flour, sea salt, celery salt, and black pepper into the butter. Gradually stir half-and-half into the mixture, taking care that no lumps form. Add lobster stock; stir. Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring constantly, until the soup begins to thicken, about 15 minutes.

Stir lobster, tomato paste, onion, and celery into the soup; season with paprika, thyme, and seafood seasoning. Continue cooking the soup to heat the onion and celery, about 10 minutes. Add cream; stir. Cook until hot, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Lobster Bisque
raw_recipe.description: This rich and creamy lobster bisque is easy to make for a nice pot of hot, savory deliciousness with plenty of lobster meat in every bite.

review.reviewBody: We thought the bisque was delicious. The only change I made was not to add any salt. When I make it again, I would use half the amount of onions and celery and sauté them in the butter before adding the flour. In addition, to lighten up the recipe and get more of that lobster flavor, I would add half the amount of cream to the flour and compensate by using more lobster stock. We enjoyed this very much.

I love this recipes so much! My daughter came home one day and said she had to make lobster bisque for her food truck project at school...I about died and said, hey, we will go to the store and buy the pre-made bisque...nope, they were sold out. So I searched and found this one. Had the ingredients except for the lobster stock and lobster...lol... That's ok, I have a recipe for poorboy lobster (using cod). 
I put the recipe together a little differently, frying the veggies in the butter and seasoning before making the roux, then the stock, then the cream, etc... I don't think it matters I just thought the liquid before the cream was a good idea.
The seasoning measurements are spot on. I tripled the recipe and freeze extra. 
In the past I used veggie stock for lobster stock (kind of salty...you have to adjust the other seasonings if you do it this way) but this time I used clam juice and cooked it down a little for the stock and stuck with the cod...I like it better than lobster and more cost efficient in my area of the country

My husband said that this is the best "soup" he's ever had in his life. He's 65 and a foody, so that's saying something. Making it again today. I made the lobster stock myself this time. (Lobster stock is hard to find so I used fish stock last time and it was still amazing.)

This was great! I used what I had on hand, so there are a few changes. It was great the first day but even better the next day! I will not add celery salt next time, with the old bay it was a little too salty. I also did not add salt. I used Better than Bullion Lobster base, perhaps it has more salt than others? I also added sherry as was done in another recipe, and I think this made the GREATEST difference and once added I realized this is the ingredient added by the 2 different restaurant seafood bisques I have enjoyed. Lastly, the seafood that I used was a bag of frozen langostino from Trader Joes (thawed) because it needed to be used and I also added shrimp. It was divine! Will definitely put this in rotation!
Very good! Husband liked it too. I did sauté onions and celery which I think was a good choice. I will make again.
I used fresh claw meat and followed the directions exactly as written. Absolutely incredible!

I Buy two whole lobsters and save the cooking water and reduce it to make the sauce. After preparing the meat put the shells back in the stock and simmer a while for a more favorful stock then drain via a colander to remove the shells. Two lobsers of a pound more more is all the meat you need. I also add a tab of butter and use cream instead of half and half but both work well, I toss in the top greens from my celery to also add flavor and remove them before serving. Do not leave the Tamale in the lobster shells when making the stock or the stock will have a green hue. (harmless)
Easy and delicious! I've made this twice now using Deb C suggestion of sautéing the onions, celery and carrots first. My husband and friend loved it and were fighting over seconds!
Very tasty and I made a variation that my hubby loves...the Old Bay Seasoning does make a difference...
